messages.content: Compare deploying a chatbot on a serverless platform versus a long-running container.

Below is a practical comparison of deploying a chatbot on a serverless platform (Function-as-a-Service, FaaS; e.g., AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, Azure Functions) versus a long-running container (e.g., Docker on ECS/EKS/GKE, Azure Container Instances, a VM). I focus on typical chatbot workloads (API endpoints that call models or model APIs, possibly with some state/cache, moderate concurrency, and variable traffic).

1) Cost
- Serverless
  - Pros: Pay-per-use (you pay for invocation time and memory used). Very cheap for low or spiky traffic because you aren’t billed for idle time.
  - Cons: For consistently high sustained usage, per-invocation billing can be more expensive than a reserved container/VM. Cold-start penalties can also increase effective cost if you must over-provision memory to reduce latency.
- Long-running container
  - Pros: Predictable flat costs (reserved instances or always-on containers); can be cheaper at high sustained throughput.
  - Cons: You pay for reserved compute even when idle.

2) Scalability & elasticity
- Serverless
  - Pros: Automatic rapid scaling up to many concurrent executions without manual capacity planning.
  - Cons: Platform concurrency limits and cold starts at scale; per-account throttles must be managed. External rate limits (model APIs) can become bottlenecks.
- Long-running container
  - Pros: With Kubernetes/managed container services you can autoscale via metrics (CPU, requests, custom), and scale stateful components more predictably.
  - Cons: Autoscaling typically requires tuning and might be slower to scale
